title: Best Books for RBI Grade B 2026: Phase 1 & Phase 2
meta_description: Best books for RBI Grade B 2026. Phase 1 quant, reasoning, English plus the unique Phase 2 ESI and Finance & Management books. Subject-wise, neutral guide.

hero.one_liner: RBI Grade B shares Phase 1 books with bank exams but needs special books for the Phase 2 ESI and Finance & Management papers.

intro: RBI Grade B has two written phases. Phase 1 is an objective screening like other bank exams, so the quant, reasoning, and English books overlap with IBPS and SBI.
Phase 2 is what sets RBI Grade B apart: Economic and Social Issues (ESI) and Finance & Management (F&M). These need dedicated books not used in other bank exams.
Treat Phase 1 as a qualifier you clear with standard bank books, then invest your real effort in the Phase 2 specialist papers where the selection actually happens.

reading_order.title: Phase 1 basics
reading_order.description: Quant, reasoning, English from standard bank-exam books to clear the objective screening.

reading_order.title: Phase 2 ESI
reading_order.description: Indian economy and social issues from specialist texts plus current economic news.

reading_order.title: Phase 2 F&M
reading_order.description: Finance and management theory, supplemented with RBI and financial current affairs.

subjects.name: Phase 1 (Quant, Reasoning, English)
subjects.intro: The objective screening shares its syllabus with IBPS and SBI, so the same books work.

books.title: Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations
books.author: RS Aggarwal
books.why: Standard quant for Phase 1, same as other bank exams. Add Arun Sharma for tougher DI.

books.title: A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning
books.author: RS Aggarwal
books.why: Covers all Phase 1 reasoning types with detailed solutions.

books.title: Objective General English
books.author: SP Bakshi
books.why: Standard English grammar and comprehension for the Phase 1 screening.

subjects.name: Phase 2: Economic & Social Issues
subjects.intro: ESI tests the Indian economy, growth, development, and social issues. This is where RBI prep gets specialist.

books.title: Indian Economy
books.author: Ramesh Singh
books.why: A strong, accessible base for the economy portion of ESI. Widely used by RBI aspirants.

books.title: Indian Economy
books.author: Mishra & Puri
books.why: More academic depth for the development economics topics in ESI.

books.title: Sociology
books.author: CN Shankar Rao
books.why: Covers the social issues portion of ESI that pure economy books miss.

subjects.name: Phase 2: Finance & Management
subjects.intro: F&M covers financial systems, regulators, and management theory. Pair books with current financial news.

books.title: Finance & Management (RBI Grade B Phase 2)
books.author: Subject guides (Arihant/Edutap-style)
books.why: A dedicated F&M guide for the syllabus. Always supplement with RBI's latest reports and financial current affairs, as this paper is current-heavy.

buying_tips: Do not over-invest in Phase 1 books if you already prepared for IBPS or SBI; reuse them.
Spend on the Phase 2 ESI and F&M books, since that is where RBI Grade B is actually won.
F&M and ESI are current-affairs heavy, so pair every book with RBI reports and financial news.

faqs.question: Can I use the same books for RBI Grade B and other bank exams?
faqs.answer:
For Phase 1 quant, reasoning, and English, yes, the same books work.

Phase 2 ESI and Finance & Management need dedicated books not used in IBPS or SBI.

faqs.question: What are the best books for RBI Grade B ESI?
faqs.answer:
Indian Economy by Ramesh Singh for the base, with Mishra & Puri for depth.

Add Sociology by CN Shankar Rao for the social issues portion.

faqs.question: How do I prepare Finance & Management for Phase 2?
faqs.answer:
Use a dedicated F&M guide for the theory, then layer on RBI reports and financial current affairs.

F&M is current-heavy, so books alone are not enough.

faqs.question: Is Phase 1 or Phase 2 more important?
faqs.answer:
Phase 1 only qualifies you; the selection happens in Phase 2.

Clear Phase 1 with standard bank books, then put your real effort into ESI and F&M.

faqs.question: Is Ramesh Singh enough for ESI economy?
faqs.answer:
It is a strong base, but supplement it with the Economic Survey and current economic news.

For development economics depth, add Mishra & Puri.

faqs.question: Do I need coaching for RBI Grade B?
faqs.answer:
Not necessarily. The booklist plus consistent current affairs and mock tests can be enough for self-study.

The deciding factor is depth in ESI and F&M, which disciplined reading builds.

faqs.question: How current-affairs heavy is RBI Grade B?
faqs.answer:
Very, especially ESI and F&M. Static books give the base, but RBI relies on recent economic and financial developments.

Follow RBI press releases and a good monthly compilation throughout.

faqs.question: When is the RBI Grade B 2026 notification?
faqs.answer:
The RBI Grade B notification typically comes out in the first half of the year on rbi.org.in.

Always confirm exact dates on the official RBI website, as they change yearly.

disclaimer: Book prices and editions are approximate and last checked in June 2026. Confirm the latest edition before buying. This is an independent guide and not affiliated with RBI or any publisher.
quick_answer: For RBI Grade B you need 5 core books costing about ₹3,100: RS Aggarwal quant and reasoning, SP Bakshi English for Phase 1, then Ramesh Singh's Indian Economy and a Finance & Management guide for Phase 2. The Phase 2 books are what separate this exam from other bank exams.
